claim: Mechanosensory hair cells of the zebrafish lateral line regenerate rapidly following damage.
source: Mechanosensory hair cells of the zebrafish lateral line regenerate rapidly following damage.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing a known property of zebrafish lateral line hair cells.

claim: Renewed hair cells arise from the proliferation of surrounding support cells.
source: These renewed hair cells arise from the proliferation of surrounding support cells, which undergo symmetric division to produce two hair cell daughters.
evidence: This statement is supported by references to established knowledge in the field.

claim: Support cells undergo symmetric division to produce two hair cell daughters.
source: These renewed hair cells arise from the proliferation of surrounding support cells, which undergo symmetric division to produce two hair cell daughters.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the mode of division of support cells.

claim: Support cells have the ability to replenish themselves.
source: Given the continued regenerative capacity of the lateral line, support cells presumably have the ability to replenish themselves.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of continued regenerative capacity.

claim: Novel transgenic lines were used to identify support cell populations with distinct progenitor identities.
source: Utilizing novel transgenic lines, we identified support cell populations with distinct progenitor identities.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the methodology and findings of the study.

claim: Support cell populations show differences in their ability to generate new hair cells during homeostasis and regeneration.
source: These populations show differences in their ability to generate new hair cells during homeostasis and regeneration.
evidence: This is a summary statement of experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Targeted ablation of support cells reduced the number of regenerated hair cells.
source: Targeted ablation of support cells reduced the number of regenerated hair cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an experimental result.

claim: Progenitors regenerated after targeted support cell ablation in the absence of hair cell damage.
source: Furthermore, progenitors regenerated after targeted support cell ablation in the absence of hair cell damage.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an experimental observation.

claim: Distinct support cell populations are independently regulated by Notch signaling.
source: We also determined that distinct support cell populations are independently regulated by Notch signaling.
evidence: This is a direct statement of a finding from the study.

claim: The existence of independent progenitor populations could provide flexibility for the continued generation of new hair cells under a variety of conditions throughout the life of the animal.
source: The existence of independent progenitor populations could provide flexibility for the continued generation of new hair cells under a variety of conditions throughout the life of the animal.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential functional significance of the findings.

claim: The zebrafish lateral line system has long been recognized as an excellent model for studying regeneration.
source: The zebrafish lateral line system has long been recognized as an excellent model for studying regeneration.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific consensus.

claim: The sensory organ of the lateral line, the neuromast, is comprised of mechanosensory hair cells organized on the surface of the head and body.
source: The sensory organ of the lateral line, the neuromast, is comprised of mechanosensory hair cells organized on the surface of the head and body (Thomas et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Lateral line hair cells regenerate rapidly following damage, with the system returning to quiescence after regeneration is complete.
source: Lateral line hair cells regenerate rapidly following damage, with the system returning to quiescence after regeneration is complete (Harris et al., 2003; Hernández et al., 2007; Ma et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The surrounding nonsensory support cells serve as progenitors for new hair cells.
source: The surrounding nonsensory support cells serve as progenitors for new hair cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field.

claim: Hair cell replenishment is proliferation-dependent and occurs symmetrically, with each progenitor dividing to give rise to two daughter hair cells.
source: This replenishment is proliferation-dependent and occurs symmetrically, with each progenitor dividing to give rise to two daughter hair cells (Wibowo et al., 2011; Mackenzie and Raible, 2012; López-Schier and Hudspeth, 2006; Romero-Carvajal et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Support cell proliferation that follows hair cell death occurs mainly in the dorsal and ventral compartments of the neuromast.
source: First, the support cell proliferation that follows hair cell death occurs mainly in the dorsal and ventral compartments of the neuromast (Romero-Carvajal et al., 2015), indicating that progenitor identity is spatially regulated.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Progenitor identity is spatially regulated.
source: First, the support cell proliferation that follows hair cell death occurs mainly in the dorsal and ventral compartments of the neuromast (Romero-Carvajal et al., 2015), indicating that progenitor identity is spatially regulated.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of spatially restricted proliferation.

claim: The most peripheral support cells, often called mantle cells, do not proliferate in response to hair cell damage.
source: The most peripheral support cells, often called mantle cells, do not proliferate in response to hair cell damage (Ma et al., 2008; Romero-Carvajal et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The regenerative capacity of the neuromast is not diminished over multiple regenerations.
source: Second, the regenerative capacity of the neuromast is not diminished over multiple regenerations (Cruz et al., 2015; Pinto-Teixeira et al., 2015), indicating that progenitor cells must also be replaced in addition to hair cells.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Progenitor cells must be replaced in addition to hair cells.
source: Second, the regenerative capacity of the neuromast is not diminished over multiple regenerations (Cruz et al., 2015; Pinto-Teixeira et al., 2015), indicating that progenitor cells must also be replaced in addition to hair cells.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of sustained regenerative capacity.

claim: Lateral line hair cells undergo turnover and replacement under homeostatic conditions.
source: Finally, in addition to regeneration in response to acute damage, lateral line hair cells undergo turnover and replacement under homeostatic conditions (Cruz et al., 2015; Williams and Holder, 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: It remains unknown whether there are distinct support cell populations within the neuromast.
source: However, it remains unknown whether there are distinct support cell populations within the neuromast (e.g. hair cell progenitors and those that replenish progenitors), as well as how progenitor populations are regulated.
evidence: This is a statement identifying a gap in knowledge that the study aims to address.

claim: CRISPR was used to generate novel transgenic lines in which distinct, spatially segregated populations of support cells are labeled in vivo.
source: In this study, we have used CRISPR to generate novel transgenic lines in which distinct, spatially segregated populations of support cells are labeled in vivo.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the methodology used in the study.

claim: Fate mapping studies using these lines show that these populations are functionally distinct with respect to their ability to contribute new hair cells during homeostasis and to generate hair cells after damage.
source: Fate mapping studies using these lines show that these populations are functionally distinct with respect to their ability to contribute new hair cells during homeostasis and to generate hair cells after damage.
evidence: This is a summary statement of experimental findings.

claim: Targeted ablation of one of these populations significantly reduces hair cell regeneration.
source: We also show that targeted ablation of one of these populations significantly reduces hair cell regeneration.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an experimental result.

claim: Support cell populations can replenish each other in the absence of hair cell damage.
source: Other fate mapping studies show that these support cell populations can replenish each other in the absence of hair cell damage.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an experimental finding.

claim: Notch signaling differentially regulates these populations.
source: Finally, we show that Notch signaling differentially regulates these populations.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an experimental finding.

claim: There are a number of distinct progenitor populations within lateral line neuromasts that are independently regulated.
source: These results demonstrate that there are a number of distinct progenitor populations within lateral line neuromasts that are independently regulated, providing flexibility for hair cell replacement under a variety of circumstances.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the study's conclusions.

claim: The majority of support cell proliferation occurs during the first twenty-four hours following hair cell death.
source: Previous studies have shown that the majority of support cell proliferation occurs during the first twenty-four hours following hair cell death (Ma et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: F-ara-EdU has been shown to be far less toxic than BrdU.
source: We replicated this finding by administering a pulse of F-ara-EdU (EdU), which has been shown to be far less toxic than BrdU (Neef and Luedtke, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: In neomycin-treated larvae, roughly 78% of regenerated hair cells were EdU-positive, compared to 6% in mock-treated larvae.
source: In neomycin-treated larvae, roughly 78% of regenerated hair cells were EdU-positive, compared to 6% in mock-treated larvae (Figure 1B–C; p<0.0001).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: At 72 hours post treatment, 28% of EdU-positive cells remained support cells.
source: We noticed that at the same timepoint that 28% of EdU-positive cells remained support cells (Figure 1E and B arrowheads).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: EdU-positive support cells may represent hair cell progenitors that had been replaced via proliferation.
source: We hypothesized that these cells may represent hair cell progenitors that had been replaced via proliferation.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on their observations.

claim: Support cells that divide after the first ablation can serve as hair cell progenitors after subsequent damage.
source: Of the 90 neuromasts analyzed, 14 retained EdU labeling. Within these 14 neuromasts, we observed hair cells after the second regeneration that were both EdU- and BrdU-positive (Figure 1G–J, arrowheads; 1.50 ± 1.45 hair cells per neuromast; mean ±SD), indicating that support cells that divide after the first ablation can in fact serve as hair cell progenitors after subsequent damage.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Support cells that divided after the first round of damage do not always serve as hair cell progenitors.
source: However, we also observed double-positive cells that remained support cells (Figure 1K–N, arrowheads; 1.07 ± 0.73 support cells per neuromast; mean ±SD), as well as support cells that were only labeled by EdU (Figure 1G–N, asterisks). These observations indicate that support cells that divided after the first round of damage do not always serve as hair cell progenitors (or even as progenitors at all).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: There is evidence of proliferation-mediated replenishment of hair cell progenitors by support cells in the neuromast.
source: Altogether, these data provide evidence of proliferation-mediated replenishment of hair cell progenitors by support cells in the neuromast, but also suggest that new hair cells arise from a pool of progenitors that are not strictly defined by their proliferation history.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the findings from the double ablation experiment.

claim: New hair cells arise from a pool of progenitors that are not strictly defined by their proliferation history.
source: Altogether, these data provide evidence of proliferation-mediated replenishment of hair cell progenitors by support cells in the neuromast, but also suggest that new hair cells arise from a pool of progenitors that are not strictly defined by their proliferation history.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: CRISPR-mediated transgenesis was employed to target expression constructs to genes that had been shown to be differentially expressed in support cells.
source: As part of a broader screen to be described elsewhere, we employed CRISPR-mediated transgenesis (Kimura et al., 2014; Ota et al., 2016) to target expression constructs to genes that had been shown to be differentially expressed in support cells (Jiang et al., 2014; Steiner et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement of the methodology used, supported by citations.

claim: Targeted insertion in sfrp1a results in expression restricted to the most peripheral support cells.
source: During this screen, we found that targeted insertion in three genes (sfrp1a, tnfsf10l3, and sost) resulted in distinct spatial expression in primary neuromast support cells: a transgene inserted in the sfrp1a locus is restricted to the most peripheral support cells (Peripheral cells; Figure 2A);
evidence: This is a direct statement of an experimental observation, supported by Figure 2A.

claim: Insertion in tnfsf10l3 is more broadly expressed throughout the periphery but is enriched in anteroposterior support cells.
source: insertion in tnfsf10l3 is more broadly expressed throughout the periphery but is enriched in anteroposterior support cells (AP cells; Figure 2C);
evidence: This is a direct statement of an experimental observation, supported by Figure 2C.

claim: Insertion in sost is limited to the dorsal and ventral support cells.
source: and insertion in sost is limited to the dorsal and ventral support cells (DV cells; Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an experimental observation, supported by Figure 2E.

claim: Secondary neuromasts are oriented orthogonally to primary neuromasts.
source: Secondary neuromasts are oriented orthogonally to primary neuromasts (Lopez-Schier et a., 2004);
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The position of the distinct support cell populations are correspondingly rotated in secondary neuromasts.
source: we found that the position of the distinct support cell populations are correspondingly rotated (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an experimental observation, supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: GFP labeling in hair cells was not observed in stable lines.
source: We did not observe GFP labeling in hair cells in stable lines (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an experimental observation, supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: At 5 dpf, 19% of hair cells were labeled with Eos expressed by the Peripheral cell transgene, and this number remained the same by 8 dpf.
source: At 5 dpf, 19% of hair cells were labeled with Eos expressed by the Peripheral cell transgene, and this number remained the same by 8 dpf (Figure 2B; p=0.7047).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Eos from the AP cell transgene labeled about 6% of hair cells at both 5 and 8 dpf.
source: Eos from the AP cell transgene labeled about 6% of hair cells at both 5 and 8 dpf (Figure 2D; p=0.9668).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Neither Peripheral nor AP cell populations are responsible for generating new hair cells under homeostatic conditions.
source: Since there is no change over the three-day span, neither of these populations are responsible for generating new hair cells under homeostatic conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing no change in labeling over time.

claim: The amount of hair cells labeled with photoconverted Eos from the DV cell transgene increased from 39% to 56% over a three-day span.
source: In contrast, the amount of hair cells labeled with photoconverted Eos from the DV cell transgene increased from 39% to 56% over that three-day span (Figure 2F; p<0.0001).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The DV cell population is predominantly involved in ongoing hair cell generation during homeostasis.
source: Thus, the DV cell population seems to be predominantly involved in ongoing hair cell generation during homeostasis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing increased labeling over time.

claim: Only 4% of regenerated hair cells were derived from the Peripheral cell population.
source: Only 4% of regenerated hair cells were derived from the Peripheral cell population, whereas the AP cell and DV cell populations contributed significantly more, generating 20% and 61% of regenerated hair cells, respectively (Figure 3B–D, arrowheads; Figure 3E; p=0.003 [Peripheral vs. AP], p<0.0001 [Peripheral/AP vs. DV]).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The AP cell population contributed 20% of regenerated hair cells.
source: Only 4% of regenerated hair cells were derived from the Peripheral cell population, whereas the AP cell and DV cell populations contributed significantly more, generating 20% and 61% of regenerated hair cells, respectively (Figure 3B–D, arrowheads; Figure 3E; p=0.003 [Peripheral vs. AP], p<0.0001 [Peripheral/AP vs. DV]).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The DV cell population contributed 61% of regenerated hair cells.
source: Only 4% of regenerated hair cells were derived from the Peripheral cell population, whereas the AP cell and DV cell populations contributed significantly more, generating 20% and 61% of regenerated hair cells, respectively (Figure 3B–D, arrowheads; Figure 3E; p=0.003 [Peripheral vs. AP], p<0.0001 [Peripheral/AP vs. DV]).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: There were about half as many Peripheral cells relative to the other two populations at 5 dpf, prior to hair cell ablation.
source: There were about half as many Peripheral cells relative to the other two populations, but no significant difference between the number of AP cells and the number of DV cells (Figure 3F; Peripheral = 14.30 ± 4.17; AP = 22.8 ± 4.40; DV = 23.86 ± 4.45; p<0.0001 [Peripheral vs. AP/DV], p>0.9999 [AP vs. DV]).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: There was no significant difference between the number of AP cells and the number of DV cells at 5 dpf.
source: There were about half as many Peripheral cells relative to the other two populations, but no significant difference between the number of AP cells and the number of DV cells (Figure 3F; Peripheral = 14.30 ± 4.17; AP = 22.8 ± 4.40; DV = 23.86 ± 4.45; p<0.0001 [Peripheral vs. AP/DV], p>0.9999 [AP vs. DV]).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The difference in regenerative capacity between these populations is not simply a reflection of the number of available cells, but rather of differences in the progenitor identity of the populations.
source: Thus, the difference in regenerative capacity between these populations is not simply a reflection of the number of available cells, but rather of differences in the progenitor identity of the populations.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data comparing cell numbers and regenerative contributions.

claim: Notch-mediated lateral inhibition plays a crucial role in ensuring the proper number of hair cells are regenerated.
source: Notch-mediated lateral inhibition plays a crucial role in ensuring the proper number of hair cells are regenerated, and inhibition of Notch signaling following hair cell damage dramatically increases the number of regenerated hair cells (Ma et al., 2008; Wibowo et al., 2011; Romero-Carvajal et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Inhibition of Notch signaling following hair cell damage dramatically increases the number of regenerated hair cells.
source: Notch-mediated lateral inhibition plays a crucial role in ensuring the proper number of hair cells are regenerated, and inhibition of Notch signaling following hair cell damage dramatically increases the number of regenerated hair cells (Ma et al., 2008; Wibowo et al., 2011; Romero-Carvajal et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: After Notch inhibition, there were roughly twice as many hair cells as control fish in all three transgenic lines.
source: In all three lines, after Notch inhibition (Neo/LY) there were roughly twice as many hair cells as control fish (Neo) (Figure 4A–B,E–F,I–J; p<0.0001 [all lines]), consistent with previous studies.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The small number of Peripheral cell-derived hair cells was no different between LY-treated fish and non-treated fish.
source: The small number of Peripheral cell-derived hair cells was no different between LY-treated fish and non-treated fish (Figure 4C; 0.62 ± 1.28 [Neo] vs. 1.15 ± 2.16 [Neo/LY]; p=0.2481).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The number of nlsEos-positive hair cells from DV cells doubled in LY-treated fish.
source: Moreover, while the number of nlsEos-positive hair cells derived from DV cells doubled in LY-treated fish (Figure 4K; 7.40 ± 2.13 [Neo] vs. 15.25 ± 6.36 [Neo/LY]; p<0.0001),
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 4K.

claim: Hair cells derived from AP cells increased roughly five-fold in LY-treated fish.
source: those derived from AP cells increased roughly five-fold (Figure 4G; 2.22 ± 1.94 [Neo] vs. 11.38 ± 4.23 [Neo/LY]; p<0.0001).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The percentage of hair cells derived from DV cells decreased after Notch inhibition.
source: As a consequence, the percentage of hair cells derived from DV cells decreased correspondingly (Figure 4L; 67.86 ± 14.63 [Neo] vs. 54.69 ± 14.01 [Neo/LY]; p<0.0001),
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 4L.

claim: The percentage of hair cells derived from AP cells doubled after Notch inhibition.
source: whereas those derived from AP cells doubled (Figure 4H; 25.19 ± 21.72 [Neo] vs. 50.68 ± 19.23 [Neo/LY]; p<0.0001).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Generation of hair cells from both the AP and DV populations is regulated by Notch signaling, with the AP population being regulated to a greater extent.
source: These data suggest that generation of hair cells from both the AP and DV populations is regulated by Notch signaling (with the AP population being regulated to a greater extent), whereas Peripheral cells are not responsive to Notch signaling.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on Notch inhibition.

claim: Peripheral cells are not responsive to Notch signaling.
source: These data suggest that generation of hair cells from both the AP and DV populations is regulated by Notch signaling (with the AP population being regulated to a greater extent), whereas Peripheral cells are not responsive to Notch signaling.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing no change in Peripheral cell contribution after Notch inhibition.

claim: The DV cell population generates roughly 60% of regenerated hair cells.
source: Since the DV cell population generates roughly 60% of regenerated hair cells, we sought to determine whether these cells were required for hair cell regeneration.
evidence: This is a summary of a previously stated finding.

claim: A transgenic line was generated in which an enhanced-potency nitroreductase fused to GFP was introduced into the sost locus using CRISPR.
source: To this end, we generated a transgenic line in which an enhanced-potency nitroreductase (epNTR; Tabor et al., 2014) fused to GFP was introduced into the sost locus using CRISPR (Tg[sost:epNTR-GFP]w216, hereafter known as sost:NTR-GFP).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the methodology used, supported by a citation.

claim: Nitroreductase is a bacterial enzyme that selectively binds its prodrug Metronidazole, converting Mtz into toxic metabolites that kill the cells expressing it.
source: Nitroreductase is a bacterial enzyme that selectively binds its prodrug Metronidazole (Mtz), converting Mtz into toxic metabolites that kill the cells expressing it (Curado et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: At three dpf, all NTR-GFP+ cells were also positive for nlsEos, while an additional subset of cells expressed nlsEos alone.
source: At three dpf, soon after the initiation of transgene expression, we see considerable overlap between NTR-GFP and nlsEos. All NTR-GFP +cells were also positive for nlsEos, while an additional subset of cells expressed nlsEos alone.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an experimental observation.

claim: At five dpf, the size of the double-positive (NTR-GFP+; nlsEos+) population did not change, whereas the number of cells expressing nlsEos alone increased significantly.
source: When we compared expression at five dpf, the size of the double-positive (NTR-GFP+; nlsEos+) population did not change, whereas the number of cells expressing nlsEos alone increased significantly, occupying a more central location (Figure 5A–B, arrowheads; Figure 5C; NTR-GFP/nlsEos: 9.04 ± 2.39 [3 dpf] vs. 8.47 ± 2.27 [5 dpf]; nlsEos only: 6.10 ± 2.27 [3 dpf] vs. 10.86 ± 2.72 (5 dpf); p>0.9999 [NTR-GFP/nlsEos], p<0.0001 [nlsEos only]).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Both transgenes initiate expression at the same time, but nlsEos protein is retained longer than NTR-GFP protein as cells mature.
source: These observations are consistent with the idea that both transgenes initiate expression at the same time, but that nlsEos protein is retained longer than NTR-GFP protein as cells mature and as a result, NTR-GFP is expressed in a subset of DV cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental observations.

claim: Treatment with 10 mM Mtz for 8 hr was sufficient to ablate the majority of NTR-GFP cells.
source: We next tested to the efficacy of DV cell ablation at 3 and 5 dpf. Treatment of these fish with 10 mM Mtz for 8 hr was sufficient to ablate the majority of NTR-GFP cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an experimental result.

claim: Treating fish with Mtz for 8 hr at five dpf slightly but significantly decreased the number of support cells solely expressing nlsEos by about 13%.
source: Treating fish with Mtz for 8 hr at five dpf (Mtz5) slightly but significantly decreased the number of support cells solely expressing nlsEos by about 13%.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment.

claim: Treating fish with Mtz for 8 hr at three dpf, followed by a second 8 hr Mtz treatment at five dpf decreased the number of solely nlsEos-positive cells by about 40%.
source: Treating fish with Mtz for 8 hr at three dpf, followed by a second 8 hr Mtz treatment at five dpf (Mtz3/5) decreased the number of solely nlsEos-positive cells even further, by about 40% (Figure 5D–G; Mock: 11.18 ± 2.04; Mtz5: 9.72 ± 2.03; Mtz3/5: 6.76 ± 2.12; p=0.0288 [Mock vs. Mtz5], p<0.0001 [Mock vs. Mtz3/5, Mtz5 vs. Mtz3/5]).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The Neo/Mtz5 treatment resulted in a small but significant reduction in both hair cells and nlsEos-positive hair cells per neuromast relative to normal regeneration.
source: The Neo/Mtz5 treatment resulted in a small but significant reduction in both hair cells and nlsEos-positive hair cells per neuromast relative to normal regeneration (Figure 6B–C,E–F; Total hair cells: 11.73 ± 2.10 [Neo] vs. 9.33 ± 1.88 [Neo/Mtz5]; p=0.0001; nlsEos+ hair cells: 7.78 ± 2.36 [Neo] vs. 4.90 ± 2.02 [Neo/Mtz5]; p=0.0003).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The Mtz3/Neo/Mtz5-treated larvae exhibited even fewer hair cells per neuromast.
source: The Mtz3/Neo/Mtz5-treated larvae exhibited even fewer hair cells per neuromast (Figure 6D,E; 11.73 ± 2.10 [Neo] vs. 7.52 ± 1.74 [Mtz3/Neo/Mtz5]; p<0.0001),
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 6.

claim: nlsEos-labeled hair cells decreased to a mere 14% of total regenerated hair cells after Mtz3/Neo/Mtz5 treatment.
source: with nlsEos-labeled hair cells decreased to a mere 14% of total regenerated hair cells (Figure 6G; 65.81 ± 14.89 [Neo] vs. 14.29 ± 18.10 [Mtz3/Neo/Mtz5]; p<0.0001).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Mtz treatment of siblings without the sost:NTR-GFP transgene had no impact on hair cell regeneration.
source: Importantly, Mtz treatment of siblings without the sost:NTR-GFP transgene had no impact on hair cell regeneration (Figure 6—figure supplement 1; Neo: 9.5 ± 1.50; Mtz3/Neo/Mtz5: 9.98 ± 1.51; p=0.2317).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from a control experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Transgenes had no obvious effect on hair cell development or regeneration in the absence of Mtz either alone or in combination.
source: Transgenes also had no obvious effect on hair cell development or regeneration in the absence of Mtz either alone or in combination (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a statement of a control experiment result, supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Ablation of DV cells reduces the number of hair cells regenerated.
source: Thus, ablation of DV cells reduces the number of hair cells regenerated.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on DV cell ablation.

claim: The number of regenerated hair cells increased significantly after LY treatment in all groups.
source: As expected, the number of regenerated hair cells increased significantly after LY treatment in all groups (Figure 7B–F; p<0.0001),
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 7.

claim: DV cell ablation significantly decreased hair cell regeneration.
source: and DV cell ablation significantly decreased hair cell regeneration (Figure 7B,D,F; 9.42 ± 1.85 [Neo] vs. 6.86 ± 1.76 [Mtz3/Neo/Mtz5]; p=0.0058).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 7.

claim: LY treatment following Mtz ablation resulted in significantly fewer regenerated hair cells than LY alone.
source: However, LY treatment following Mtz ablation resulted in significantly fewer regenerated hair cells than LY alone (Figure 7C,E,F; 21.08 ± 4.42 [Neo/LY] vs. 15.06 ± 3.51 [Mtz3/Neo/Mtz5/LY]; p=0.0029),
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Inhibiting Notch signaling cannot fully compensate for the loss of the DV population.
source: indicating that inhibiting Notch signaling cannot fully compensate for the loss of the DV population.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data comparing Notch inhibition with and without DV cell ablation.

claim: Roughly 88% of regenerated hair cells were nlsEos positive when larvae expressed both tnfsf10l3:nlsEos and sost:nlsEos transgenes.
source: When we crossed the tnfsf10l3:nlsEos and sost:nlsEos lines together, we found that roughly 88% of regenerated hair cells were nlsEos positive when larvae expressed both transgenes, compared to 65% from sost:nlsEos alone and 28% from tnfsf10l3:nlsEos alone (Figure 8A–E; p<0.0001).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiment, supported by data shown in Figure 8.

claim: The AP population is distinct from the DV population in terms of its progenitor function.
source: Thus, while not completely additive, these data suggest that the AP population is distinct from the DV population in terms of its progenitor function.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on combined transgene expression.

claim: Mtz-ablated larvae had significantly fewer hair cells than non-ablated larvae.
